niche.diet: Carnivore: flesh of Cuarteta, Brújula, drifting carcass fragments, and salt-rich detritus.

links: Avoids snagging in tidal kelp and lava crevices
Turbid shallows (F20) + rapid tidal flux (F13) demand 3D agility

skill.effect: The creature darts through murky shallows without stirring the silt, gliding swiftly past obstacles.

chains.weakness: Cannot stop quickly on hard rock; slides into spines and loses balance
observe: Sees it coil in submerged tuff shadows at noon
Uncoils silently when the first light hits the water
Leaves only a gentle ripple where the glassy shallows part

journal.en: It moves like water itself, leaving only a ripple where the shallows part.

plausibility.summary: A ~1.9 m, ~11 kg anguilliform body is consistent with a shallow, structure-loving fish-predator: high length-to-mass keeps maneuver volume high in turbid 3D habitat (F20) while fitting tidal flux and lava-tube mouths (F9, F13). Limb reduction matches colonization of crevices and algal mats rather than open shelf; 1.05 g (F2) slightly favors lateral undulation over sustained sprinting in 1.6× drag (F4), which fits ambush 'Silt Glide' logic.
fixes: A ~1.9 m, ~11 kg anguilliform body is consistent with a shallow, structure-loving fish-predator: high length-to-mass keeps maneuver volume high in turbid 3D habitat (F20) while fitting tidal flux and lava-tube mouths (F9, F13). Limb reduction matches colonization of crevices and algal mats rather than open shelf; 1.05 g (F2) slightly favors lateral undulation over sustained sprinting in 1.6× drag (F4), which fits ambush 'Silt Glide' logic.

analogues.organism: Moray and snake eels (Gymnothorax, ophichthids): undulatory swimming in reefs, tide pools, and burrows; avoid open water, hunt from cover.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Ampullae of Lorenzini-like electroreceptors along snout
links: Detects muscle twitches of hidden prey
Turbidity limits sight (F20) while wave noise (F4) masks pressure cues

skill.effect: The creature detects the faint outline and quick movements of hidden prey nearby, allowing it to track them easily.

chains.weakness: Overloaded by lightning storms (F10), causing panic strikes and self-harm
observe: Sees head tilt toward specific water columns
Strikes a precise point in zero-visibility water

journal.en: It hunts by the spark of a heartbeat. The dark water is no cover at all.

plausibility.summary: Treat storm sensitivity as disorientation and missed strikes (or retreat to tuff/lava cover before convection storms), not reliable self-injury; describe receptors as gel-filled pores on snout/rostrum, not 'antennae' (use barbels or lateral pit lines in observe text).
fixes: Treat storm sensitivity as disorientation and missed strikes (or retreat to tuff/lava cover before convection storms), not reliable self-injury; describe receptors as gel-filled pores on snout/rostrum, not 'antennae' (use barbels or lateral pit lines in observe text).

analogues.organism: Bull and hammerhead sharks in murky estuaries (Carcharhinus leucas, Sphyrna spp.): ampullae of Lorenzini for prey geomagnetic/bioelectric cues in low visibility.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Prey aggregate in shallows at low light
Tidal drawdown (F13) concentrates prey; 26 h day (F3) extends twilight

skill.effect: The creature strikes strongly in dim light, but its attacks grow weak and inaccurate under bright sunlight.

chains.weakness: Blind to sudden flashes, relies entirely on electro/pressure cues
observe: Hides in rock overhangs during midday heat
Emerges with the first fog and falling tide
Tracks the movement of secondary predators, not plants

journal.en: It waits for the fog to lift and the tide to turn. Then the shallow waters boil.

plausibility.summary: Long civil twilight (~38 min per transition, thick-air scattering, F3) plus spring-neap tidal cycling (F13, F6) gives repeatable windows when small predators filter/feed and are concentrated at channel edges—classic ambush scheduling. Island radiation (F27) allows a specialist twilight shallow predator without contradicting D26 rarity of large carnivores: at 11 kg Morrudo is mid-tier, not apex. Dawn fog (F8/F16) shifts reliance to vibration/electro cues, matching stated foraging mode.
fixes: Long civil twilight (~38 min per transition, thick-air scattering, F3) plus spring-neap tidal cycling (F13, F6) gives repeatable windows when small predators filter/feed and are concentrated at channel edges—classic ambush scheduling. Island radiation (F27) allows a specialist twilight shallow predator without contradicting D26 rarity of large carnivores: at 11 kg Morrudo is mid-tier, not apex. Dawn fog (F8/F16) shifts reliance to vibration/electro cues, matching stated foraging mode.

analogues.organism: Twilight-active inshore piscivores (e.g. barracuda Sphyraena, snook Centropomus): peak activity at low light; tidal flats concentrate prey at ebb.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: High pO2 (D10) supports metabolic cost; dense air (F4) cools dawn pools

skill.effect: Its thick, gelatinous skin shields it from freezing conditions, allowing it to keep striking strongly in the cold.

chains.weakness: Vulnerable to gill parasites (F29) if dermal layer is torn by rock spines
observe: Basks on submerged basalt at noon, skin glistening
Salt crystals form on its flanks as it rests
Skin feels like wet rubber, not scaly

journal.en: Its skin holds the sea’s warmth like a bladder. Strike it, and you fight a cold, wet rock.

plausibility.summary: Limit pronounced gel to snout canal bed and electrosensory dermatotomes; keep flank musculature for 'Low Light Lunge'; weakness: torn skin/gill pockets raise parasite load (F29), not vague dermal 'stiffness' only.
fixes: Limit pronounced gel to snout canal bed and electrosensory dermatotomes; keep flank musculature for 'Low Light Lunge'; weakness: torn skin/gill pockets raise parasite load (F29), not vague dermal 'stiffness' only.

analogues.organism: Skates and rays (Rajiformes): gel-filled electroreceptor canals; temperate eels remain muscular with modest subcutaneous gel, not bathypelagic consistency.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

relations.note: Eats dissolved proteins and small prey from the shallows
Ambushes it when it filters suspension near the shore
Becomes prey when the terrestrial predator wades into the shallows to drink

body_plan.origin: Undulatory swimmer; limbs reduced for navigating lava-tube entrances and floating algal mats

temperament: Ambush predator, highly reactive to vibrations, avoids open water
secrets: Luminescent gut contents: digested carcass bits glow faintly through its belly, revealing recent kills.
moments: When the tide recedes over the causeway, it coils in the shallowest glass, waiting for the first shadow to cross the water. It does not blink. It only listens.

journal.en: It moves like water itself, leaving only a ripple where the shallows part.
It waits for the fog to lift and the tide to turn. Then the shallow waters boil.
